purpose: Identify current saved-world CPU/render bottlenecks; diagnostics only, no gameplay optimization applied.

save.name: New World
save.source_writes: None. The entire live world directory was copied before running; region-cache writes target only this copy.

method.camera: Restored saved camera, held still. Save does not store open-window state, so inspection windows remain closed.
method.warmup: Wait for terrain jobs/initial earthworks, then 120 unmeasured train updates at 1/60 s.
method.native: world phases without fixed use the game real-time delta and original bounded substep loop.
method.controlled: world-fixed phases advance exactly 1/60 s per rendered frame, isolating drawing changes from extra fractional physics substeps.
method.visibility_controls: Only scene visibility/shadow flags change; routes, trains and simulation remain loaded. Bridge/track/support types in the save are not changed.
method.probes: New scopes remain disabled during ordinary gameplay. Probes=false runs verify measurement overhead.

findings.finding: Real-time slow frames execute two complete train substeps, including scene transform/running-gear application twice before one rendered frame.
findings.evidence: Native: 2 substeps and 12 per-train visual applications per frame, train.update mean 8.395 ms. Fixed 1/60 control: 1 substep, 6 visual applications, mean 5.375 ms. Native uninstrumented frame mean 20.596 ms (about 48.6 frames/s equivalent).
findings.next: Keep physics and reservation semantics, but accumulate visual changes and apply final car/bogie transforms and running-gear distance once per rendered frame.

findings.finding: Signals generate excessive draw submissions and repeat unchanged native scene updates.
findings.evidence: Hiding signal geometry reduces fixed-control draw calls from about 3437 to 2048 and frame mean from 18.56 to 15.54 ms. SignalRenderer itself costs about 1.93 ms per native frame while resetting all 209 poles, lamps and arrows.
findings.next: Cache positions/aspects/arrow visibility and use shared instanced signal geometry by kind/material, retaining picking and per-signal identity.

findings.finding: Sleepers perform LOD native calls on every track batch even when the camera and tracks are unchanged.
findings.evidence: Track rendering update costs about 1.48 ms per native frame. UpdateSleeperLod always sets VisibleInstanceCount and Visible for each batch. Hiding sleepers changes only about 31 draw calls in this saved view, so their drawing is not the main problem here.
findings.next: Skip unchanged LOD writes and camera-stationary passes; invalidate affected batches after track/origin changes.

findings.finding: Main-thread allocation churn contributes to spikes.
findings.evidence: Native uninstrumented run allocates about 762762 bytes per frame on the main thread. In the instrumented native run, 18/300 frames contain a gen0 collection: mean 26.45 ms versus 20.47 ms on other frames. Instance synchronization allocates roughly 167 KB per fixed frame.
findings.next: Reuse per-frame batch/transform buffers and cached integer/template keys rather than rebuilding dictionaries, lists and formatted strings.

findings.finding: Long-range shadow rendering is a significant additional GPU cost.
findings.evidence: Fixed controls submit roughly 10 million primitives including shadow passes; all-shadows-off control submits about 3.27 million. Tree-shadow-only removal submits about 7.04 million, and terrain-shadow-only removal about 7.28 million.
findings.next: Keep nearby shadows; investigate tighter caster distance/LOD, static geometry batching and terrain shadow policy instead of disabling all shadows.

findings.finding: Current bridges, cargo and industries are not the primary steady-frame bottlenecks in this save.
findings.evidence: Native industry update averages 0.008 ms and cargo synchronization 0.001 ms. Hiding the five bridge segments does not improve measured mean frame time in its run. Industry visibility removal changes about 32 draw calls.
findings.next: Prioritize the measured train/track/signal work before changing these systems.

limitations: This is a current-save diagnosis, not a comparison against an older commit on the identical save; it cannot identify a particular historical regression.
GPU timing and total frame timing vary with clocks, scheduling and scene evolution. Visibility control timings are individual observations, not additive or guaranteed savings.
CPU scope timings are nested and overlap; GPU and CPU work overlap as well. Do not sum all columns.
Allocated-byte counters cover the current main thread only, excluding worker/native/GPU allocations. GC correlation does not establish the cause of every slow frame.
The camera stays still after streaming settles. Camera movement, initial loading, editing terrain and extra inspection viewports can add costs not measured here.
The measured viewport is 1280x800; larger resolutions and different hardware may change the balance.

reproduce.fixed_control: Use --phase=world-fixed; suffixes -nosignals, -notracks, -nosleepers, -nobridges, -notrains, -noindustries, -notrees, -noshadows, -noterrainshadows, -notreeshadows isolate rendering. Add --probes=false to disable scopes.
reproduce.warning: Always copy the saved world first, including regions; the full-world harness can write region cache files in the directory passed through --save.
